html:
Russia's state controlled gas company, formed in 1989 when the Soviet Ministry of the Gas Industry was turned into a corporation under Viktor Chernomyrdin. The name is short for "gas industry" in Russian.

It holds some of the largest gas reserves in the world and the pipelines that carried Soviet and then Russian gas west. For decades it was Europe's main gas supplier, and Germany in particular built its industry on cheap pipeline gas, later through Nord Stream under the Baltic Sea.

Under Vladimir Putin the state took back firm control, and gas became a tool of foreign policy. Price disputes with Ukraine cut supplies to much of Europe in 2006 and 2009. After Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, Gazprom cut deliveries, the Nord Stream pipes were blown up, and Europe turned to other suppliers and liquefied gas by ship. Gazprom lost its biggest market.
